spans.text: Pupa is a local AI workbench: hand a goal to the agent, and it breaks the task down, calls tools, and delivers results. Files and threads stay on this machine.

Type in the input box and press the send key (Enter by default; can be changed to Ctrl+Enter in settings).
The agent streams its reply; tool calls appear in the

Screenshots, recordings, and other multimodal inputs are supported and are sent to the agent along with the message.

The model switcher beside the input box affects only the
; the default configuration is left untouched. Once a thread is created, its system prompt and model stay fixed within that thread.
All conversation data is stored in a local SQLite database; you can browse past threads while offline.
The main window has three areas: the
on the left carries the thread list and main entries; the middle is the
, showing message bubbles and the working process; the bottom is the
, with model switching and send controls.
Tool calls and intermediate output stream into the
collapsible bar in real time as the agent works. Each tool entry is labeled on the right with its context usage and execution time, for example
The trajectory view replays a task's full execution timeline round by round, including model reasoning, tool calls, and context compaction events — use it to inspect how a complex task ran.
For everyday use the working process is enough; open the trajectory view when you need a full review.
Every message you send counts as 1
; every action the model performs (a model call, a tool call, or the final reply) counts as 1
. A single task can span multiple user rounds and multiple model rounds.
To the model, everything is a tool. The agent calls tools as needed while running a task; each call appears in the working process in real time, labeled with its context usage and duration.
When the context nears its limit, the system compacts the history automatically and shows a compaction card. Context usage drops noticeably afterwards, and the task can continue.
Complex tasks are broken down and handed to subagents. A subagent is a work unit the main agent creates on the fly; its execution appears in the working process as tool entries.
A thread's system prompt stays frozen after it is first created; long-term memory is injected once at thread initialization, keeping the model's prompt cache stable.
Add and manage models under the
category in settings. Each model can be configured independently with its key, service address, and parameters.

spans.text: One model record can hold separate parameters for chat (LLM), speech recognition (ASR), speech synthesis (TTS), image generation, and video generation. Fill in what you need.
Before saving, use the "Probe" button to verify that the context length or voice list is available.
page in settings centrally manages the capabilities the agent can call, split into tabs for built-in tools, MCP tools, skills, knowledge bases, and more.
Built-in tools: local capabilities shipped with the app, such as file read/write and terminal execution.
MCP tools: external tools connected through MCP servers.
Skills: capability extension packages organized as resources.
Knowledge base: long-term knowledge retrieval for the agent.
Local capabilities run under least privilege: system capability calls must be declared explicitly and are never silently exposed to remote ends.
Pupa stores file assets in a local workspace directory. The
setting specifies the root path; files the agent produces and content you export are both saved locally.
Files, screenshots, and generated content from a session can be viewed and managed in the file panel, with drag-and-drop interop with the system file manager.
Put the workspace on a disk partition with plenty of space, and back up important output regularly.

Use the screenshot entry in the input area to capture the screen, or paste or drag images straight into the input box. Images are sent to the agent along with the message, for recognition and understanding.

Hold the record button in the input area to start recording; on release the audio is transcribed into the input box, and you can send it once confirmed. Speech recognition uses the service configured in
Once a TTS voice is configured, the agent's replies can be read aloud; with image and video generation parameters configured, the agent can call those capabilities during a task to produce content.
Multimodal capabilities depend on the corresponding parameters being filled in; unconfigured items do not appear in the input area.
The settings page is organized by category; the search box at the top locates a category by keyword.

spans.text: Language, theme, and font size changes take effect immediately; no restart needed.
Conversation history, tool records, and configuration are stored in a local SQLite database.
File assets are stored in the local workspace directory; see "Files & Workspace".
Offline, you can still browse past threads; network is only needed to start a conversation or call online services.
Model requests go directly to the service address you configured; Pupa does not handle or store them through any third-party relay.
To back up, copy both the database file and the workspace directory to preserve conversations and file assets in full. Use the same approach when migrating to a new device.
Exported diagnostics (see "Diagnostics & Troubleshooting") contain only key-free information about this machine's settings and capability counts, for troubleshooting.

under the Help category in settings; the app writes key-free local settings and capability counts into a diagnostics file, for troubleshooting. A popup shows the file location once the export finishes.

Check that the key and service address in the model configuration are correct, and confirm this machine can reach the service. The "Probe" button quickly tells you whether it is a network problem or a parameter problem.
Usually a request timeout or network instability. Raise the timeout in the model configuration and retry; the portion already generated is kept in the thread.

Expand the working process bar above the message and check the output and duration of the failed entry — in most cases the cause is immediately visible (path does not exist, insufficient permissions, service not running, and so on).
This means the task's context is large. Raise the model's "Max context" parameter, or split the long task across several threads.
When troubleshooting execution problems, the trajectory view replays every step round by round.
